description:
Write, debug and learn Go on iPhone and iPad. GopherForge brings an on-device Go compiler, multi-file editor, tests, offline React study builds, source debugging and a Go course together. Compile, run, test, vet and format with bundled Go 1.27.1. Compatible downloaded projects run without a connection.

CODE AND DEBUG
• Edit Go, go.mod and web sources with highlighting, a line-number gutter and keyboard shortcuts.
• Tap a Go line number for a breakpoint. Run starts source debugging when breakpoints exist; otherwise it runs normally.
• Continue, Step Into, Over and Out; inspect project call stacks, source locations and current-frame locals.
• Follow diagnostics to source and inspect tests, Output, images and concurrency timelines.
• Import GitHub commit snapshots or Files content; export, favorite, tag and search projects. Choose a local or Files/iCloud library.

PLAYGROUND WITH PEOPLE AND AI
• Create a temporary online room or join through an Edit/View link. Share bounded text sources and device-reported Output without an app account.
• Connect a compatible Claude or Codex MCP client to read, edit and request Run/Test. Native Run/Test executes only on the device whose user presses it. Other participants receive Output and never automatically execute remote edits.
• Keep local drafts, review conflicting revisions, save an independent project copy and leave a room. The owner can close it. Rooms expire and can end on a server restart; they are not backups.
• AI access requires your chosen client/provider and shared capability. No AI model, subscription or quota is included. Browser participants edit and read Output; browser Go execution is not provided.

REACT + GO, OFFLINE
Build browser JS, JSX, TypeScript, TSX, CSS and local JSON with bundled esbuild WASI and a fixed React catalog. Use Build & Preview or documented offline npm commands. Study deterministic in-memory Gin APIs through bounded local request replay.
This is an educational builder: no full Node.js/npm runtime, Bun, arbitrary scripts, Vite plugins or registry downloads. TypeScript is transpiled without type checking. API state is temporary; no network listener is started.

LEARN GO AND PREPARE FOR INTERVIEWS
• 220 teaching lessons, including 173 worked readings, plus 22 prediction challenges across 28 units.
• Values, collections, interfaces, errors, generics, modules, concurrency, runtime, standard library and production contracts.
• Four architecture/clean-code units with 40 lessons; 23 classic patterns and six concurrency/resilience patterns.
• Around Go: Bash, Git, Docker, Kubernetes, MongoDB, Redis, Gin, blockchain infrastructure and service security.
• Practical Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, agent and MCP workflows: scoped edits, isolated execution, validation and source ownership.
• 132 interview guides across 15 topics and four levels; twelve interactive algorithm labs with 36 scenarios.
• Continue, editable lesson drafts, Review, Fix mistakes and independent interview marks. Explicitly publish a read-only progress snapshot for a friend or AI. The unlisted link expires after 90 days or earlier revocation; no automatic app/web progress sync.

Native layouts adapt to iPhone, iPad and supported Duo postures, touch and external keyboards. Themes, text size and supported Face ID/passcode locking. One paid download; no subscription, ads or app account. Ordinary projects/progress stay local; optional rooms and published snapshots upload only their selected content.

Go uses bounded WebAssembly/WASI: no guest networking, cgo or general shell. Ordinary Run has no guaranteed CPU Stop. Module ZIPs allow up to 4,000 files. Imports/missing packages need a connection. Source debugging covers project code; no watches or conditional breakpoints. Stop needs a project checkpoint. Isolated frontend previews block external requests; legacy HTML previews may load linked resources. Database/deployment lessons describe external native workflows.

Guide: https://gopherforge.app/guide
promotionalText: Go on your device. Share a Playground with people or a compatible Claude/Codex MCP client, run locally, and share a read-only learning progress link.
whatsNew:
• New Playground rooms for people and compatible AI clients. Share Edit/View links, text files and device-reported Output without an app account.
• MCP tools for reading/editing sources, requesting Run/Test and reading a published progress snapshot. A request never runs code by itself: the native user presses Run/Test on their own device.
• Publish a read-only learning progress link with lesson and interview marks, Continue places and a readable JSON view. Preview first; revoke it or let it expire after 90 days.
• Keep local room drafts and Output across relaunch, review revision conflicts, leave a room and save an independent project copy.
• Expanded agent/MCP explanations in the existing AI lessons and interview guides. The 220 teaching lessons, 22 challenges, 132 interview guides and existing saved progress remain available.
• Online collaboration is optional. Ordinary compatible Go projects and the bundled React study builder continue to run locally and offline.
reviewNotes:
GopherForge 1.3.2 (51). No app account, sign-in or demo credentials. Release automatically after approval. Existing on-device Go/React tools and learning remain available offline. New collaboration and explicitly published progress use HTTPS at gopherforge.app; internet is needed only for those optional features.

PLAYGROUND: Projects > Playground · people & AI. Local starter main.go is available before any room. Tap Run: the bundled WASI compiler executes on this iPhone/iPad. Expand Room & AI connection > Create a one-hour room. This intentionally sends the displayed text files. Share Edit or View link, or open the room on another device. Only an explicit native Run/Test invokes the local compiler; peers receive device-reported Output, revision and device label. Joining, polling, remote edits and AI run requests never execute code automatically. Leave room keeps local source/last Output. Save an independent project copy creates a new library identity. Owner Close ends the room.

MCP: public Streamable HTTP endpoint https://gopherforge.app/mcp. No OAuth/account or included AI model. Four tools: playground_read, playground_write, playground_request_run, learning_progress_read. Room tools require the Edit/View capability from the room link in tool input or Bearer auth. View cannot write/request. Claude/Codex configuration and mobile-compatible remote connectors are documented at https://gopherforge.app/guide/mcp. An AI request remains pending until the native person presses local Run/Test; this preview does not offer browser Go execution or cloud compilation. Files/Output are untrusted text, not automatic instructions.

PROGRESS: Learn > Share progress > preview > Publish read-only link. Only whitelisted lesson IDs, reported compiler marks, interview self-assessments and Continue IDs are uploaded; no source, drafts, attempts, names or device identifiers. Unlisted link is readable HTML plus JSON for AI tools, expires after 90 days or earlier Revoke. It is a snapshot, not account sync. Opening preview does not upload. Native app/web progress remain separate. Existing IDs and progress formats are retained.

PRIVACY: optional room text, participant label and reported Output live in bounded server memory until displayed expiry (normally 1h) or earlier restart/closure; not E2E encrypted or backup. Progress snapshots persist until expiry/revocation. Holding a capability grants its role; give AI only the intended Edit/View link, never owner/revocation keys or private projects. Infrastructure access logs support delivery/security/aggregate operational reporting. No advertising/tracking SDK, app account, subscription or IAP. Privacy: https://gopherforge.app/privacy

REGRESSION: 14 focused native contract/content checks passed, including real bundled Go execution on one seat while another observed without running, independent explicit second-seat execution, UTF-8 draft relaunch and Leave/relaunch. Two Release UI checks passed for a fresh local Run and progress preview without publication. Web contract tests and the official MCP SDK client passed discovery/read/write/role/run-request checks. Compatible actual Claude/Codex account/mobile configurations depend on the user's provider; no universal account certification is claimed.

LIMITS: Go 1.27.1 runs in bounded WASI, no guest networking/cgo/general shell; ordinary Run lacks a guaranteed tight-loop CPU Stop. Source-debug Stop requires own-source checkpoints. Offline npm is a fixed educational esbuild/React builder, not full Node/npm/Bun or arbitrary scripts. Gin replay uses bounded httptest, not a listener. Full guide: https://gopherforge.app/guide
